text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former Government of Singapore Investment Corporation manager Eddie Taw Cheng Kong was found guilty on eight charges of corruption after a 15-day trial.

- The new Housing Board measures will rid the HDB market of opportunistic demand and allow it to meet the housing needs of those, especially first-time applicants, who need it most, property analysts and MPs said.
- The Singapore dollar will make its debut on the New York Cotton Exchange next month in a landmark development that could irk the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
- Thailand has weathered the worst of its recent economic downturn, and while recovery is imminent, people must be patient, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said.
- Chinese enterprises are more satisfied with the performance of joint ventures in China when their foreign partners appoint top management.
- The benchmark SES-Property Index closed at a two-week low following government measures announced over the weekend to shorten the waiting time for first-time applicants for Housing Board flats.

- Demand for HDB resale flats and lower-end condominiums is likely to be boosted by the latest measures to shorten queues for new Housing and Develoopment Board flats, developers and consultants said.
- Property stocks held up reasonably well following Sunday's new HDB rules.
- The new 10-year waiting period for a second new HDB flat may goad HDB upgraders to opt for private property after five years, say the more bullish analysts.

- The Monetary Authority of Singapore has called on financial institutions to review their computer systems and has issued guidelines to ensure that financial institutions here are not affected by the "Millennium Bug".
- Although earnings of listed motor companies have obviously been squeezed lately because of rising COE prices, leading players have managed to maintain healthy margins.
- SIA subsidiary SilkAir has confirmed a BT report that it is buying eight aircraft from Airbus Industries' A319/320 family worth about US$420 million.
- Shangri-la Hotels and Resorts, one of Asia's largest hotel chains, has signed a contract to manage a hotel in Seoul, its first hotel management job in South Korea.
- Tye Soon made a creditable debut on the main board, giving shareholders a 55 percent gain on the first day of trading.
- Neptune Orient Lines, which is in the midst of a US$825 million takeover of U.S. shipping group APL, has appointed four new non-executive directors.
